papers.title: REM Sleep Iota Oscillations Across the Lifespan
papers.abstract: Iota oscillations are a newly discovered marker of wakefulness and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. So far, iota in REM sleep has only been reported in the surface electroencephalography (EEG) of a small sample of young adults and in intracranial recordings of epileptic patients. Here, we investigated the presence of these oscillations in a large dataset (N=937) of high-density sleep EEG recordings from individuals 7 to 70 years old. We found that iota spectral peaks during REM sleep were between 25 and 40 Hz, slightly faster than in wake (25-35 Hz). Iota power was significantly associated with REM sleep architecture, increasing with both REM duration and across progressive sleep cycles. Iota peaks were observed in individuals of all ages, although the prevalence decreased gradually with age, from 88% in children to 44% in older adults. Most iota spectral peak properties (frequency, amplitude, timing, topography) likewise shifted with age. The most striking effect, however, was in bandwidth, such that children had narrow iota peaks, older adults had broad iota peaks, and 20-30 year olds could have either. It remains unclear whether narrowband and broadband iota are functionally equivalent. On shorter time scales (< 1 year), iota properties remained stable across measurements. Analyses of a separate dataset of monozygotic and dizygotic twins revealed high heritability of all iota peak properties except bandwidth. Overall, these results establish iota as a genetically determined trait-like marker of REM sleep with unique age-related changes. Iota oscillations open new avenues to investigate the interaction between sleep, genetics, development, and aging.

papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) triggers characteristic changes in the cortical electroencephalogram (EEG) during waking and sleep, as well as upregulating molecular signatures of neuronal activity, synaptic plasticity, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. This includes the induction of the unfolded protein response (UPR), the primary marker and adaptive mechanism of ER stress. Yet how cortical neuronal activity during SD contributes to the induction of these molecular signatures remains unknown. Here we investigate whether manipulating cortical activity during SD with a physiological stimulation paradigm (flickering light stimulation, FLS) affects the induction of the UPR. As expected, SD alone upregulated activity-dependent and UPR-related genes in cortex and led to increased EEG slow-wave activity (SWA) during subsequent NREM sleep, an electrophysiological signature of sleep need. Delivering FLS during SD, however, prevented the upregulation of activity- and UPR-related genes while inducing an additional increase in SWA during subsequent sleep. Further analysis of neuronal firing revealed that FLS induced brief neuronal silent (OFF) periods in awake animals during stimulation, thereby shifting cortical activity towards a brain state resembling sleep. These findings suggest that physiological manipulation of cortical activity during waking is sufficient to dissociate molecular signatures of ER stress from electrophysiological markers of sleep pressure. We propose that global sleep wake history and cortical network dynamics differentially regulate activity-dependent transcription and the accumulation of sleep pressure.

papers.title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
papers.abstract: Propofol anesthesia is widely used for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, but electroencephalographic (EEG) features of anesthetic state transitions in this brief and stimulus-rich setting remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe clinically interpretable EEG markers across anesthetic stages using portable polysomnography (PSG)-derived six-channel EEG. In this prospective observational study, 31 adults undergoing GI endoscopy under propofol-based anesthesia underwent continuous portable PSG recording. EEG analyses focused on six scalp channels (F3, F4, C3, C4, O1, and O2) across four clinically defined stages: baseline, induction, maintenance, and recovery. Relative spectral power, spectral edge frequency at 95% cumulative power (SEF95), and spindle-like event metrics were quantified. Sensor-level functional connectivity was assessed using weighted phase-lag index, imaginary coherence, and amplitude envelope correlation (AEC). Spectral and spindle-like event measures were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, and connectivity differences were assessed using permutation-based paired tests with false discovery rate correction. Relative delta power decreased from baseline and induction to maintenance and recovery, whereas theta, alpha, sigma, and beta relative power and SEF95 generally increased. Spindle-like event density differed across stages and was highest during recovery, while mean duration and peak frequency remained relatively stable within the 11-16 Hz range. Functional connectivity showed metric-specific modulation: AEC demonstrated the most widespread stage-related differences, whereas phase-based connectivity measures showed only limited edge-specific changes after correction for multiple comparisons. Portable PSG-derived six-channel EEG captured stage-related spectral, spindle-like event, and sensor-level connectivity changes during propofol anesthesia for GI endoscopy. These findings identify candidate EEG features for future evaluation of emergence detection and atypical anesthetic-state identification during procedural anesthesia. Their utility for real-time propofol titration or excessive-sedation warning requires prospective validation.

Amplitude envelope correlation showed the most widespread stage-related connectivity differences, identifying candidate EEG markers for emergence detection and atypical anesthetic-state identification.

papers.title: Comparing re-referencing methods for human intracranial EEG
papers.abstract: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) involves the implantation of depth electrodes in the brain to monitor epileptic seizures for surgical feasibility. As the electrodes advance into deeper limbic structures, the macro contacts distributed along the shaft record electrical activity from more lateral sites, while a bundled array of microwires simultaneously captures highly localised signals from the tip of the electrode. In a clinical setting these electrical signals are recorded relative to a reference signal, which may be sub-optimal for subsequent analyses that are unrelated to clinical objectives. Therefore, a secondary re-referencing operation is often undertaken to transform the signal in relation to a specific hypothesis. Despite a recent surge in SEEG studies, comparative studies on the much-understudied issue of re-referencing are sparse. Here, we analyse data collected from 16 human patients during an episodic memory task and comparatively apply a range of re-referencing methods to both macro contact and micro-wire data. We find that the choice of method changes the proportion of trials that survive artefact rejection, low frequency power, and the aperiodic background against which that power is read. In the hippocampal recordings, however, no method differed from any other in the size of a memory effect in power or spike-field coherence. This early transformative decision therefore bears on how the signal is described. We found no evidence that it changes the detectability of the behavioural effects tested here, and no method reversed the direction of a memory effect.

ai.reason: Systematic comparison of re-referencing choices affecting artifact rejection and power/aperiodic background; highly transferable to signal normalization across recording systems.
ai.summary: This study compared re-referencing methods on macro-contact and microwire SEEG data from 16 epilepsy patients performing an episodic memory task, finding that method choice altered artifact-rejection survival, low-frequency power, and aperiodic background. In hippocampal recordings, however, no method changed the magnitude or direction of the memory effect in power or spike-field coherence.

papers.title: Dynamics-informed machine learning for recovering extensive missing systems dynamics.
papers.abstract: Inevitable missing values in observational time series often hinder reliable data-driven modeling of complex systems across diverse domains. Recovery is essential yet challenging, particularly in high-dimensional systems where most variables can exhibit extensive intra-series missingness and widespread inter-variable missingness simultaneously. In this study, we introduce a dynamics-informed imputation framework, termed Full-Partial Reconstruction Mapping (FPRM). In contrast to traditional approaches that directly fit time series interdependences, the FPRM embeds intrinsic dynamical priors via state-space reconstruction and recovers multiple incomplete series by learning diffeomorphic topology between attractors from complete and incomplete data. We validate the FPRM on paradigmatic model systems (e.g., an ecology system, the ordinary Lorenz system, a coupled 120-dimensional (120D) Lorenz system, and a coupled 120D Rössler system and real-world datasets (e.g., road occupancy rate from transportation system, electroencephalogram (EEG) signals from neuroscience, exchange rates from finance, and wind speed from climate systems). Even in high-dimensional systems where only one variable is fully observed and all others suffer from extreme missingness (e.g., 90%), the FPRM enables reliable imputation of multiple incomplete variables-a task that challenges most existing approaches. This dynamics-guided framework outperforms traditional approaches, alleviating substantial data gaps and enabling robust data-driven paradigms for complex dynamical systems.

ai.reason: State-space/dynamical reconstruction for missing time series, validated on EEG, is methodologically transferable and reproducible.
ai.summary: The authors introduce Full-Partial Reconstruction Mapping (FPRM), a dynamics-informed imputation framework that embeds state-space reconstruction priors and learns diffeomorphic topology between attractors from complete and incomplete data. Across model systems (including coupled 120D Lorenz and Rössler systems) and real datasets, FPRM reliably imputed multiple variables even when only one variable was fully observed and others had up to 90% missingness, outperforming traditional approaches.

papers.title: Beyond Mean Pooling: Statistical Meta-Aggregation for Subject-Level EEG Classification in Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a non-invasive, temporally precise tool for studying neural alterations associated with Parkinson's disease (PD). When labels are defined at the subject level but inputs are epoch level, a key design choice is how epoch-wise predictions are aggregated to a single subject-level decision. Most prior work uses mean pooling, which assumes all epochs contribute equally and independently. This study proposes a statistical meta-aggregation strategy that represents each subject by 14 descriptors of the epoch-wise prediction distribution, including measures of central tendency, dispersion, shape, and high-confidence concentration. Using a self-supervised contrastive encoder trained on task-evoked EEG from the Simon conflict task, and a sample of 90 subjects including 57 PD and 33 control, this work evaluates the proposed framework under subject-wise five-fold cross-validation. Replacing mean pooling with statistical meta-aggregation lifts subject-level ROC-AUC from 0.655 to 0.872 for logistic regression and from 0.724 to 0.840 for support vector machines, without modifying the encoder or the classifier family. Averaging predictions across three independent self-supervised pretraining seeds yields competitive performance and improved balanced accuracy. These results suggest that, in this dataset, the way epoch-level predictions are summarized at the subject level has a substantial effect on final PD classification performance.

papers.title: How Much of Cross-Subject EEG Emotion Recognition Is Stimulus Memorization?
papers.abstract: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition now reports accuracies above 90% on stimulus-defined benchmarks such as SEED, and the field has examined several ways in which such numbers can be inflated, attributing inflation to subject identity, to data partitioning, and to repeated stimulus presentation. We observe that one variable has been left out. On these datasets the emotion label is assigned to the video at design time, so any encoder that recovers which video was shown obtains the label for free. We adapt three representation-level shortcut diagnostics to a cohort of published contrastive cross-subject encoders, and find that stimulus identity is linearly recoverable at six to fifteen times chance. We then measure its impact on the reported accuracy by holding out subjects and stimuli jointly, and find that each released classifier loses two to forty-four points once the test videos are unseen, so a headline obtained under subject hold-out alone is not a measure of cross-subject emotion decoding.

ai.reason: Shortcut diagnostics and joint subject/stimulus hold-out are broadly useful for reproducible EEG classifier evaluation.
ai.summary: The authors adapted three representation-level shortcut diagnostics to published contrastive cross-subject EEG emotion encoders and found stimulus identity was linearly recoverable at six to fifteen times chance. When subjects and stimuli were held out jointly, each released classifier lost two to forty-four accuracy points, indicating that headline accuracies from subject hold-out alone reflect stimulus memorization rather than cross-subject emotion decoding.

papers.title: EEG-Based Characterization of Cortical Dynamics during Graded Resistance Exercise.
papers.abstract: Understanding how brain activity varies during voluntary movement under different resistance conditions may provide insights into neural responses associated with physical demands and inform the development of neurorehabilitation strategies. In this study, we investigated changes in neural activity associated with increasing resistance levels during unilateral bicep curl movement. Ten healthy participants performed bicep curls under five resistance conditions while their cortical activity was recorded using electroencephalography (EEG). Movement-related cortical potentials (MRCPs), power spectral density (PSD) topographies, nonparametric spatiotemporal cluster-based permutation tests and linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) were used to characterize EEG differences across resistance conditions. Differences in MR-CPs and frequency-specific power spectral density (PSD) patterns were observed across resistance conditions, with significant spatiotemporal clusters identified during pre-movement, peak contraction, and movement execution phases. A Triplet Temporal Convolutional Network (TTCN) was also employed to learn latent representations from these EEG signals, and its discriminative capability was evaluated using a k-nearest neighbors (KNN) classifier. The learned embeddings showed separation between the resistance conditions, with classification errors occurring primarily between neighboring conditions. Using a within subject leave-one-trial-out (LOTO) evaluation strategy, the TTCN-KNN framework achieved accuracy of 97.2%. Furthermore, subject-independent evaluation were conducted using a leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) approach, achieving a maximum accuracy of 93.0%. These findings suggest that EEG signals contain discriminative information for distinguishing the resistance conditions in both within-subject and subject-independent settings, providing preliminary in sights for future EEG-based monitoring of motor effort and adaptive brain-machine interface applications.

papers.title: MULTIMODAL EEG WORLD MODEL: SELF-SUPERVISED LATENT TRANSITION LEARNING FOR WEARABLE EEG SEIZURE DETECTION
papers.abstract: Existing supervised and self-supervised EEG models mainly learn within-segment discriminative or reconstructive representations, leaving transitions between adjacent EEG segments underexplored. We propose a self-supervised Multimodal EEG World Model for EEG seizure detection that predicts the latent representation of the next EEG segment from the current EEG state, conditioned on synchronized ECG, EMG, and movement signals. A learnable query-based fusion module aggregates the multimodal synchronized signals into a compact physiological condition. Pretraining uses no seizure labels; downstream detection retains only the frozen EEG encoder and a linear probe. On the SeizeIT2 dataset with a strict patient-wise split, the model achieved an AUPRC of 0.3748, ROC-AUC of 0.8025, and balanced accuracy of 0.7308, outperforming official database baselines (SVM with hand-crafted features and ChronoNet), an external baseline (DSAINet), and a foundation model (NeuroLM). Ablations show a 14.4% relative AUPRC gain over a random-initialized encoder, supporting multimodal-conditioned latent transition learning for wearable EEG representation learning.

papers.title: Daytime Napping and Associative-Memory Retrieval Speed: An Exploratory Behavioral and EEG Study
papers.abstract: Purpose: To test whether a daytime nap was associated with improved associative-recognition performance relative to monitored wakefulness and to determine where any response-time (RT) difference occurred in the RT distribution. Methods: Fifteen healthy students completed nap and wake sessions in a within-participant design. Each session included word-pair learning, immediate recognition, a 60-min interval, and delayed recognition without additional study. Trial-level log RT was the focal outcome; accuracy and electroencephalography (EEG) were complementary outcomes. Results: The RT Condition-by-Time interaction was significant (b = -0.063, 95% CI [-0.117, -0.009], p = .027). Responses were 6.7% faster after the nap (p = .010) but did not change after wakefulness (p = .704), with the difference concentrated among slower responses. Accuracy showed no condition-specific change (p = .401). Nap EEG showed aperiodic spectral slowing and stronger periodic sigma activity, but no EEG measure explained the RT effect. Conclusions: Daytime napping was associated with faster delayed associative recognition, primarily through attenuation of the slowest responses. The exploratory findings warrant larger confirmatory studies.

Nap EEG showed aperiodic spectral slowing and stronger periodic sigma activity, but no EEG measure explained the response-time effect.

papers.title: Delineating neural contributions to electroencephalogram-based speech decoding.
papers.abstract: Objective. Speech Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have emerged as a pivotal technology in facilitating communication for individuals with speech impairments. Utilizing electroencephalography (EEG) for noninvasive speech BCIs offers an accessible and affordable solution, potentially benefiting a broader audience. However, EEG-based speech decoding remains controversial especially for overt speech, due to difficulties in separating speech-related neural activities from myoelectric potential artifacts generated during articulation. Moreover, because paradigms for collecting covert speech data are inherently less scalable than those for overt speech, whether the neural dynamics underlying EEG-based decoding of overt speech are also present during covert speech remains an open and practically important question.Approach. Here we aim to delineate the extent of the neural contributions to EEG-based speech decoding, and the degree to which the underlying neural dynamics are shared across overt and covert speech, by employing Explainable AI techniques to a convolutional neural network predicting spoken words based on signals obtained by ultra-high-density (uhd)-EEG.Main results. We found that electrode-wise contributions to the decoding cannot be explained by their mutual information with electromyography (EMG). Furthermore, contributing periods of speech to EEG-based decoding are distinct from those to decoding solely relying on EMG. In contrast, there are significant overlaps in signal timings contributing to EEG-based decoding, regardless of vocal conditions such as overt or covert speech. Notably, the denoising process successfully enhanced the decoding contribution from electrodes within speech-related brain areas for all speech conditions.Significance. Altogether, our findings support the idea that, with appropriate preprocessing, EEG becomes a valuable tool for decoding spoken words based on underlying neural activities.&#xD.

papers.title: CNN-based classifier for subject-independent MBTI Extraversion/Introversion preference classification from short-time EEG signals
papers.abstract: This study examines whether short, minimally preprocessed EEG segments contain sufficient information to distinguish between individuals classified as extraverted or introverted according to the Myers--Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI). EEG recordings from 50 participants were divided into 4-s segments and analyzed using a subject-independent nested 5-fold cross-validation procedure to compare EEGNet, EEGProgress, and a newly proposed compact convolutional architecture, SSCNet. SSCNet achieved the highest mean accuracy (0.6481), AUC (0.7063), and F1-score (0.6276). The proposed architecture also showed the lowest variability across folds. SSCNet demonstrated the best computational efficiency, with the shortest median training epoch time and the highest training throughput despite having a similar number of trainable parameters to EEGProgress. The results suggest that MBTI Extraversion--Introversion preferences may be moderately predictable from short time-domain EEG segments without manual spectral feature extraction, while highlighting the importance of subject-independent validation and computationally efficient model design.

papers.title: A feature-optimized EEG framework using multiscale entropy and metaheuristic optimization for cognitive analysis.
papers.abstract: Cognitive activity plays an important role by influencing working-memory, problem-solving, attention, response and decision making. EEG serves as a non-invasive approach to analyze neural activity associated with cognitive processing. The current study aims to identify the more contributing features to analyze the cognitive activity between sports and non-sports groups. The present study included 100 participants, consisting of 80 males and 20 females aged between 19 and 23 years. EEG signals were acquired and preprocessed using filtering methods to remove unwanted noise and artifacts. The four-entropy metrics dispersion entropy, permutation entropy, sample entropy, and fuzzy entropy were applied to the coarse-graining method across multiple temporal scales to analyze the complexity of EEG signals. To identify the most informative feature subsets and reduce redundancy, filter-based methods such as Mutual Information, Pearson Correlation, Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance and wrapper-based methods such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization were applied. Finally for differentiating the cognitive activity, five machine learning classifiers that include Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, K-nearest neighbor, Decision Tree and Random Forest were applied. Statistical methods such as T-test and Fleiss kappa were used to analyse the performance efficiency. Feature extraction phase yielded a total of 160 multiscale entropy features. The entire features when fed into both filter-based and wrapper-based methods, Genetic Algorithm based optimization yielded a minimal contributing feature subset with high nested cross-validated accuracy of 93.0 ± 2.7% with Support Vector Machine. This contributing feature subset was used as input for five different machine learning classifiers for differentiating the cognitive activity between both groups. The five classifiers demonstrated high cross-validated agreement on held-out subjects, with a mean Fleiss' kappa of 0.874 ± 0.051 (95% CI: 0.811-0.937), depicting a good inter-classifier agreement for classification of samples into sports and non-sports individuals. The study demonstrates that multiscale entropy features combined with metaheuristic-based feature optimization can effectively analyze the cognitive activity between sports and non-sports individuals. The proposed EEG framework provides a structured approach for real-time cognitive activity analysis using compact and informative entropy-based feature subsets.

ai.reason: Interpretable entropy-based feature extraction and optimization is somewhat relevant to lightweight EEG analysis, though applied to cognitive group comparison rather than sleep or transfer.
ai.summary: The study applied multiscale entropy features (dispersion, permutation, sample, fuzzy) with filter- and wrapper-based feature selection to EEG from 100 participants to distinguish sports from non-sports groups. Genetic Algorithm optimization yielded a minimal feature subset with 93.0 ± 2.7% nested cross-validated accuracy using SVM, and five classifiers showed mean Fleiss' kappa of 0.874 ± 0.051.

papers.title: The spatial extent of fast ripples is associated with cognitive and language deficits in children with focal epilepsy: An exploratory SEEG study.
papers.abstract: To determine if the spatial extent of interictal fast ripples in focal epilepsy patients is associated with brain dysfunction. Thirty pediatric focal epilepsy patients who underwent SEEG investigation had their cognitive and language deficits assessed in scales of 0 to 4. Fast ripples (250-500 Hz), ripples (80-250 Hz), and IEDs were automatically detected in 10 min during NREM sleep. We fitted linear models to the relationship between the cognitive deficit scale and the spatial spread of the interictal neurophysiologic events (number of channels with rate of events > 10 % of maximum rate). For the language deficit, we computed the Spearman correlation between the median rate of events in all brain regions and the deficit scale. Cognitive deficit scale was significantly associated with the number of channels with fast ripples (p = 0.049), not so with ripples (p = 0.31), IEDs (p = 0.31). The potential confound of number of explored channels did not improve the fitting of the models. Language deficits were not correlated with the number of channels showing interictal events. However, from all brain regions the most statistically significant correlations (p < 0.01) were between median fast ripple rates in the left and right pars opercularis and triangularis of the inferior frontal gyrus (Broca's area and its contralateral counterpart) with r = 0.66, p = 0.003 (18 patients), in the superior temporal gyrus in the language dominant hemisphere with r = 0.72, p = 0.005 (13 patients), and the dominant basal temporal region with r = 0.79, p = 0.006 (10 patients). Median rates of IEDs and ripples exhibited lower correlation with language deficits in these regions. Widespread fast ripples are associated with increased cognitive deficits, and language deficiencies are correlated with fast ripple rates in brain regions associated with language. The extent of fast-ripple activity was associated with cognitive deficit severity in this cohort, whereas the corresponding associations for ripples and IEDs did not reach statistical significance.

papers.title: ADHDeepNet: An Explainable Framework for EEG-Based ADHD Detection From Raw Signals.
papers.abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common brain disorder in children that can persist into adulthood, affecting social, academic, and career life. Early diagnosis is crucial for managing these impacts on patients and the healthcare system but is often labor-intensive and time-consuming. This paper presents a novel method to improve ADHD diagnosis precision and timeliness by leveraging Deep Learning (DL) approaches and electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. We introduce ADHDeepNet, a deep learning model that utilizes comprehensive temporal-spatial characterization, attention modules, and explainability techniques optimized for EEG signals. ADHDeepNet integrates feature extraction and refinement processes to enhance ADHD diagnosis. The model was trained and validated on a dataset of 121 participants (61 ADHD, 60 Healthy Controls), employing nested cross-validation for robust performance. The proposed two-stage methodology uses a 10-fold cross-subject validation strategy. Initially, each iteration optimizes the model's hyper-parameters with inner 2-fold cross-validation. Then, Additive Gaussian Noise (AGN) with various standard deviations and magnification levels is applied for data augmentation. ADHDeepNet achieved 100% sensitivity and 99.17% accuracy in classifying ADHD/HC subjects. To clarify model explainability and identify key brain regions and frequency bands for ADHD diagnosis, we analyzed the learned weights and activation patterns of the model's primary layers. Additionally, t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) visualized high-dimensional data, aiding in interpreting the model's decisions. This study highlights the potential of deep learning and EEG in enhancing ADHD diagnosis accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction.
papers.abstract: Understanding language in real-world interaction requires methods that integrate auditory, visual, and neural signals. We present a proof-of-concept study combining mobile electroencephalography (EEG) and eye tracking to investigate referential selection during dyadic communication. Using a simplified version of the director task, pairs of participants engaged in naturalistic object-movement instructions while EEG and gaze data were recorded and synchronized via LabStreamingLayer, allowing us to calculate overlap-corrected, regression-based event-related potentials (rERPs) time-locked to spoken nouns and to participants' fixations, focusing on the N400/P300 (300-500 ms) and later (500-800 ms) time windows. Our results show that gaze behavior and fixation-related potentials provide crucial information for interpreting language-related ERPs: Targets competing with occluded referents elicited a stronger posterior positivity consistent with greater attentional demands. Fixation timing systematically modulated neural responses. Contrary to predictions, competitors received little visual attention, indicating that participants prioritized task-relevant information. These findings highlight the potential of multimodal data integration for understanding attentional and predictive mechanisms in real-world communication. Importantly, we show that established analytic techniques, such as artifact subspace reconstruction, independent component analysis, and linear deconvolution for ERP calculation, apply to noisy, naturalistic datasets. In addition, we provide a subsampling sensitivity approach to test the stability of the effects across different sample sizes. This study provides a methodological framework linking gaze and neural activity during interactive language processing. All preprocessing and analysis scripts, along with example datasets, are openly available on OSF ( https://osf.io/5ds4z ; a modified and optimized Python implementation is also available on GitHub: https://github.com/XlinCLab/DGAME ).

papers.title: EEG microstate alterations in psychotic depression: prolonged microstate C duration and associations with psychotic symptoms.
papers.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (MDD-Psy) represents a severe clinical subtype with distinct psychopathology, yet its underlying large-scale brain network dynamics, as measured by resting-state EEG microstates, remain poorly characterized. We compared 68 patients with MDD-Psy and 63 patients with MDD without psychotic features (MDD-NonPsy). Clinical assessment included the Kangduo Antidepressant Scale (KDAS) and the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS). Resting-state EEG microstate parameters (duration, time coverage, occurrence, and transition probabilities) were analyzed. Group comparisons employed Mann-Whitney U/t-tests with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction. Correlations between microstate alterations and psychotic symptom severity were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation with FDR correction. The groups were comparable in age and sex. The MDD-Psy group exhibited significantly greater severity in thought disturbance, activation, and hostility (all p < 0.001). EEG microstate analysis revealed a significantly prolonged median duration of microstate C, putatively associated with salience-network-related activity in MDD-Psy (91.99 ms) versus MDD-NonPsy (85.56 ms; p-corr = 0.004). Altered transition probabilities characterized MDD-Psy, including increased B→A but decreased B→C and C→A transitions (all p-corr < 0.05). Furthermore, in the combined sample, the duration of microstate C positively correlated with thought disturbance (ρ = 0.243, p-FDR = 0.030), while the reduced B→C transition probability was strongly negatively correlated with both thought disturbance (ρ=-0.393, p-FDR < 0.001) and hostility. Within patients with major depressive disorder, the psychotic subtype is associated with a distinct pattern of aberrant resting-state brain network dynamics relative to the non-psychotic subtype, characterized by prolonged microstate C duration, commonly linked to salience network dynamics and reconfigured temporal transitions between the salience, visual, and auditory networks. The altered visual-to-salience network transition (B → C) demonstrated the most robust association with core psychotic symptom dimensions, including thought disturbance and hostility. These findings suggest that dysregulated dynamic coupling between perceptual processing and salience evaluation may represent a candidate neurophysiological indicator of psychotic features in depression. However, these results should be considered hypothesis-generating preliminary: the high rate of antipsychotic medication use in the MDD-Psy group, the absence of a healthy control group, and the cross-sectional design preclude tentative causal or specificity claims. Future longitudinal studies incorporating medication-naïve patients, healthy controls, and complementary neurophysiological markers are required to validate the clinical utility of these microstate alterations. Not applicable.

papers.title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Accurately assessing recovery in patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness (PDoC) is essential for evaluating the therapeutic efficacy and optimizing clinical care. However, substantial individual variability and poorly understood recovery mechanisms render this task exceptionally challenging. We collected task-state electroencephalography and clinical records from 78 PDoC patients to develop an intelligent assessment framework. Power spectral densities (PSDs) and coherence values (CVs) derived from event-related potentials (ERPs) were extracted and integrated with motor function scores to construct a multidimensional feature set. Linear support vector machine (SVM) and logistic regression (LR) models were built and rigorously evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized for visual explanation. The LOOCV indicated that both LR and SVM achieved optimal, similar performance in integrating alpha-band features with motor function (Macro-Average F1-score [Ma-F]: 76.79% versus 75.54%). The Receiver Operating Characteristic curves (with Area Under the Curve values of 77.57% for LR and 72.82% for SVM) and Precision-Recall curves (with Average Precision values of 68.87% for LR and 59.85% for SVM) suggested that the framework performs stably. The reliability curves indicated that both models demonstrate good calibration and are reliable for assessment. The study provides preliminary evidence that alpha-band PSDs and CVs derived from ERPs potentially enhance the motor function assessment performance. This integrated paradigm provides a valuable indicator. Overall, our findings suggest that combining neuroscience with intelligent technology holds promise for improving personalized diagnosis and optimizing the PDoC management.

papers.title: [Spectral-topographic features of EEG in patients with varying rates of alcohol dependence progression].
papers.abstract: To compare the spectral-topographic characteristics of the background electroencephalogram (EEG) in patients with alcohol dependence, differing in disease progression rate, as part of a pilot study. A total of 40 male patients with a confirmed diagnosis of alcohol dependence (F10.2 according to ICD-10) were examined. Utilizing a retrospective evaluation of the development of alcohol withdrawal syndrome (AWS), participants were classified into two distinct groups: those exhibiting rapid progression (≤3 years, n=23) and those with slow progression (≥12 years, n=17). Background EEG recordings were obtained using a 16-channel system (10-20 configuration), followed by spectral analysis of absolute power in the theta, alpha-1, alpha-2, beta-1, and beta-2 frequency bands. The analysis revealed that patients with rapid progression demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in the spectral power of the alpha-1 rhythm across all cortical regions (p<0.002 after correction), with the most pronounced effects observed in frontal and central leads. There were also reductions noted in the power of alpha-2, theta (except the parietal region), and beta-1 (limited to the frontal area) frequency bands. Notably, 74% of patients with rapid progression exhibited a low-amplitude («flattened») EEG pattern, whereas 71% in the slow progression group maintained a normal alpha rhythm. The results indicate the presence of a distinct neurophysiological endophenotype associated with the rapid progression of alcohol dependence. Key characteristics of this endophenotype include a overall decrease in the power of the alpha-1 rhythm, particularly in the front-central leads; a decline in theta power (excluding the parietal region); a frontal-specific reduction in beta-1 power; and a significant prevalence of low-amplitude EEG patterns.

papers.title: Region-Specific EEG Classification of Hypnotic Susceptibility Using a Sliding-Window 2D CNN: A Subject-Independent Evaluation
papers.abstract: We investigate whether a 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on minimally preprocessed EEG signals can classify hypnotic susceptibility across distinct brain regions. Sixty-two male participants (32 Control, 30 Guided Imagery / Hipno group) underwent a 20-minute EEG recording using a 256-channel EGI cap. A sliding-window approach evaluates all 10-second windows within the recording for each of seven predefined brain regions (prefrontal, frontal, temporal, central, parietal, occipital, and facial), yielding up to 868 independently trained models. Initial screening with a segment-level 90/10 random split showed that five regions exceeded the 0.67 accuracy threshold, with the occipital region achieving the highest mean accuracy (0.721) across 90.3% of windows. Subject-independent evaluation via Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation, however, substantially revised this picture: occipital performance collapsed to near-chance (mean ACC 0.453, AUC 0.429), revealing that high random-split accuracy was driven by subject-specific EEG fingerprints rather than genuine group differences. In contrast, the frontal and prefrontal regions maintained above-chance LOSO accuracy (0.646 and 0.624, respectively), demonstrating genuine generalisability. These results underscore the necessity of subject-independent validation in EEG-based classification studies and highlight anterior cortical regions as more reliable neural markers of hypnotic susceptibility.

papers.title: Quantitative Analysis of Electroencephalography in Hypnosis: A Neurophysiological Approach.
papers.abstract: Hypnosis is a unique state of consciousness marked by heightened response to suggestions, focused attention, and altered cognitive control. This article explores the neural connections involved in hypnosis through electroencephalography (EEG) studies, examining brain changes during hypnosis and their relationship to hypnotic depth and susceptibility. Theta waves, linked to hypnotic depth, are stronger in highly hypnotizable individuals, while gamma waves are associated with focus, suggestion acceptance, and emotional responses. Hypnosis also induces frequency-dependent reorganization of large-scale brain connectivity, particularly in frontal-parietal and attentional networks, enhancing subjective experiences and responsiveness. EEG patterns reveal more dynamic neural activity during hypnosis, which cannot be captured by linear metrics alone. Hemispheric analysis shows greater left-hemisphere activity in highly hypnotizable individuals, particularly in emotionally and verbally mediated tasks, challenging the right-hemisphere dominance model. Event related potential (ERP) findings show that hypnosis affects information processing at both pre-attentional and cognitive levels. These insights contribute to understanding hypnosis' impact on the brain and its potential for personalized therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: EEG-Based Classification of Hypnotic Susceptibility Using Two-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Guided Imagery (GI) is a mind-based relaxation technique widely used in clinical and therapeutic settings. Objectively assessing whether a patient has entered a relaxed state remains a challenge for clinicians. This study investigates electroencephalography (EEG)-based classification of hypnotic susceptibility using two-dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (2D CNNs) applied to minimally preprocessed signals, without manual feature extraction. Data were collected from 62 male participants (32 Control, 30 Hypno) using a 256-channel dense array amplifier during Guided Imagery or cognitive task conditions. A sliding-window framework evaluated up to 868 independent models across seven anatomically defined brain regions and 124 ten-second time windows. Segment-level random-split screening was followed by Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation to obtain subject-independent performance estimates, and an ensemble approach combined predictions across K = 10 windows. The best single-window model achieved accuracy of 0.82 on the random split. Under LOSO, anterior regions generalised better across subjects: the frontal region achieved mean accuracy of 0.646 (AUC: 0.692). An ensemble of K = 10 windows further improved the prefrontal region to mean accuracy of 0.738. The occipital region, dominant in random-split screening, collapsed to near-chance under LOSO, revealing subject-specific EEG fingerprinting rather than genuine group differences. Bandpass filtering and z-score normalisation suffice for competitive EEG classification without manual feature extraction. Anterior cortical regions are identified as the most generalisable neural markers of hypnotic susceptibility.

papers.title: Advanced Detection of Pre-Ictal Stages in Epilepsy Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Automated Feature Extraction.
papers.abstract: During a seizure, the neurons in the brain are firing abnormally. It is important to identify the symptoms to stop the spread of the virus, as a late diagnosis greatly increases the risk of infecting others. The domain is still heavily biased towards the use of just a few publicly available scalp EEG datasets (for instance, CHB/MIT) and has barely scratched the surface in relation to the use of iEEGs with little consideration for multi-centre or private datasets. Class imbalance, where preictals outnumber interictals and icts, also presents a challenge in the training process due to the non-stationarity, variability, and presence of noise in the EEG data. The study used the pre-processed data and the convolution neural network model to predict the duration of the pre-ictal phase of an epilepsy attack. To this end, the CHB-MIT gathering dataset is used. Hand-crafted features usually work with conventional methods. The suggested approach comprises signal metadata processing, an automatic feature extraction tool supported by signal characteristic identification and LSTM and SVM-based result classification. The proposed model defines the pre-ictal state considering sensitivity and specificity. Initially the detection system was configured for a two-second window duration.

papers.title: Variable task difficulty with augmented sensory feedback for motor training in virtual reality.
papers.abstract: This study examined how motor task difficulty and augmented sensory feedback (ASF) modality influence task performance, physiological responses, and perceptual experience during virtual reality (VR)-based upper-limb motor training. Building on related brace- and VR-based ASF platforms previously examined in neurotypical and spinal cord injury cohorts, the long-term goal is to support neurorehabilitation-oriented adaptive VR training; however, the present study used neurotypical participants as an initial validation step. Fourteen right-handed neurotypical participants used a supportive upper-limb brace and surface electromyography (EMG) for myoelectric control of a virtual robotic arm in a two-dimensional tracking task. A 2 × 2 within-subject design crossed ASF modality (visual feedback versus visual + haptic feedback) with task difficulty (straight-line versus sinusoidal trajectory). Outcomes included normalized path length, task completion time, movement jerk, alpha- and beta-band electroencephalogram (EEG) power over motor cortex, heart rate, EMG amplitude, EMG-displacement-based virtual work, and perceptual ratings of agency, motivation, and utility. Short-term pre-to-post percentage changes were computed for each measure. VHF straight-line training produced the largest reductions in normalized path length (-4.69%) and completion time (-6.12%), whereas VHF sinusoid training produced the largest reductions in movement jerk (-5.67%) and virtual work (-13.33%). ASF modality affected path length, completion time, jerk, EMG amplitude, and virtual work, whereas task difficulty modulated beta-band EEG power and the physiological index. Changes in path length were positively associated with changes in completion time and EMG amplitude. These findings suggest that ASF modality and task difficulty can differentially shape short-term behavioral, physiological, and perceptual responses in healthy participants. The exploratory distribution of participant-specific best-case conditions motivates future studies using independent trial subsets to evaluate whether behavioral and physiological measures can support individualized VR training.

papers.title: Mobile EEG Reveals Age-Dependent Cognitive-Motor Interference with Increasing Motor Task Complexity- a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study examined age-related differences in behavior and brain dynamics underlying cognitive-motor interference (CMI) during motor dual-tasks (DT) with increasing motor task complexity. Behavioral performance and electrocortical activity were assessed in 19 younger adults (11 males, 8 females; 25.5 ± 2.3 years) and 11 older adults (6 males, 5 females; 72.6 ± 4.6 years) using mobile electroencephalography (EEG). Participants performed an oddball choice-reaction task under three conditions: sitting, standing, and treadmill walking. Event-related potential (ERPs; P1, N1, P3) amplitudes and latencies, response times, postural sway, and gait parameters were recorded to evaluate CMI. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVAs with within-subject factors of motor condition and stimulus type and age group as a between-subject factor. Older adults exhibited reduced step length compared to younger adults, but no DT-related changes in gait or postural sway were observed. Response times were generally slower in older adults and increased from sitting to standing and walking whereas younger adults showed slowing only from sitting to standing. Early sensory ERP components (P1, N1) demonstrated increased amplitudes with higher motor demands. The P3 component was reduced in amplitude in both groups during walking, with delayed latencies in older adults. For both groups, P3 latencies were associated with prolonged response times. Our findings suggest that this slowing during walking reflects altered cognitive resource allocation, characterized by delayed central information processing and enhanced early visual processing, rather than impaired peripheral motor coordination.

papers.title: Generalized Spike-Wave discharges and myoclonic features in a subgroup of children with Self-Limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes.
papers.abstract: Generalized spike-wave discharges (GSWD) are occasionally observed in patients with self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), but their clinical significance remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize the electroclinical features of these patients and to explore their potential clinical implications. We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of 148 children diagnosed with SeLECTS at Xuanwu Hospital from June 2015 to October 2025. Patients with GSWD on electroencephalography were identified and compared with those without GSWD regarding demographic characteristics, seizure semiology, auxiliary examination findings, treatment response, and outcomes. GSWD were identified in 9 of 148 patients (6.1 %) with SeLECTS. These 9 patients included 4 males and 5 females, with a median onset age of 8 (IQR: 5-10) years. Compared with those without GSWD, they more frequently showed wakefulness seizures (44.4 % vs 5.8 %, p < 0.05), generalized tonic-clonic seizures during sleep (44.4 %), and myoclonic manifestations (77.8 %). Other clinical variables were similar between groups. All 9 patients achieved freedom from focal and generalized tonic-clonic seizures, though one required prolonged combination therapy. Two patients with follow-up exceeding 10 years showed electroclinical evolution toward juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, characterized by the absence of centrotemporal spikes, with generalized spike-wave bursts recurring on later EEGs. We identified a subgroup of patients with SeLECTS characterized by the coexistence of GSWD and myoclonic features, showing partial electroclinical overlap with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy. These findings broaden the electroclinical spectrum of SeLECTS, though the relationship between focal and generalized network dysfunction in this subgroup requires confirmation in larger, prospectively followed cohorts.

papers.title: EEG-defined differences in functional networks following beta-band transcranial alternating current stimulation in patients with disorders of consciousness: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Severe disruption of cortico-thalamocortical circuits underlies disorders of consciousness (DOC). Beta-band (20 Hz) transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) can be used to probe frontal oscillatory synchrony, yet its potential to acutely modulate large-scale network dynamics in DOC is unknown. We applied 20 Hz tACS (1 mA) for 30 min over the frontal cortex (F3 and F4, International 10-20 system) in 28 patients with DOC. Offline functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was used to quantify hemoglobin (HbO)-based functional connectivity (FC) and graph-theoretical network properties, including small-world properties (clustering coefficient, Cp; path length, Lp) and global efficiency (global efficiency, Eg; local efficiency, Eloc) at pre-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (pre-stim), the first post-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (post-stim1), and the second post-stimulation resting-state measurement for 5 min (post-stim2). Subgroups were defined by baseline video-electroencephalography (vEEG) pathology as moderately abnormal (n = 11) and diffuse slowing (n = 14); 3 patients excluded (incomplete vEEG). Frontal 20 Hz tACS was associated with transient enhancement of FC across the measured cortical network at post-stim1 (pFDR < 0.05), selectively strengthening intra-and interhemispheric and intra-nodal connectivity before resolving by post-stim2. Crucially, the effects were pathology-dependent, and visual-motor integration pathways (right occipital lobe to left motor cortex; right primary somatosensory cortex to left occipital lobe) emerged exclusively in DOC patients with moderately abnormal background but not in those with diffuse slowing. Concurrent acute network reorganization at post-stim1 (all p < 0.05) featured increased Cp, Eg, and Eloc, along with decreased Lp, all normalizing by post-stim2. Clinically, Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores correlated positively with average FC of HbO (pre-stim: r = 0.47; post-stim2: r = 0.41) and Area Under the Curve (AUC) of Eg (pre-stim: r = 0.44), and negatively with AUC of Lp (pre-stim: r = - 0.41; all p < 0.05). Frontal beta-tACS was associated with state-dependent changes in functional network organization in DOC, with dynamic fNIRS measures that may be useful for tracking these changes. These findings provide preliminary descriptive evidence of short-term network changes associated with beta-tACS and may help guide future controlled studies of targeted neuromodulation in patients with DOC.

papers.title: [Neurocognitive characteristics in children with sluggish cognitive tempo].
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to assess the neurocognitive characteristics of children diagnosed with sluggish cognitive tempo (SCT) and to evaluate the efficacy of Cortexin in addressing this condition. The main study group included 40 children aged 12 to 14 years with symptoms consistent with SCT manifestations. The comparison group consisted of 30 children with combined ADHD (ADHD-C), also aged 12 to 14 years. The control group comprised 30 children in the same age range without any neuropsychiatric disorders. The study used several methods, including S. Lee's SCT scale for assessing the severity of SCT symptoms, the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI-20), the Daytime Sleepiness Scale, and T.A. Fotekova and T.V. Akhutina's reading skills assessment method, the «Working Memory» method to quantifying working memory capabilities, the TOVA computer test, and EEG (routine and spectral analysis). Cortexin was administered intramuscularly at a standard dosage of 10 mg every other day across 10 injections to patients diagnosed with SCT. The study results showed that children with SCT, in comparison to their counterparts with ADHD-C and healthy peers, exhibited significantly more pronounced asthenic symptoms and a higher prevalence of comorbid learning disorders. Quantitative EEG analysis revealed a reduced theta-to-alpha wave power ratio in the anterior cerebral cortex of the SCT group compared with the ADHD cohort. These findings support the hypothesis that children with SCT are less prone to exhibiting deficits in inhibition processes, while instead demonstrating a decline in overall levels of functional activity maintenance. A follow-up assessment after treatment revealed improvements in inattention, severity of working memory impairment, asthenic symptoms, and reading skills in 82% of cases. Additionally, EEG analysis post-treatment indicated a reduction in alpha-band power in the frontal and central leads of both hemispheres, suggesting enhanced overall cortical activation. This study has delineated several cognitive characteristics associated with SCT in children and demonstrated that administering Cortexin significantly alleviates the primary symptoms of SCT and mitigates the manifestation of major comorbid disorders.

papers.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
papers.abstract: Pharmacotherapy is recommended as the first-line treatment for adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), yet some individuals show partial or inadequate response associated with adverse effects. These limitations have prompted interest in adjunctive or alternative interventions. Electroencephalography (EEG) neurofeedback is a non-pharmacological intervention for ADHD, which enables self-regulation of neural activity. This systematic review synthesised clinical, cognitive, and electrophysiological outcomes of EEG neurofeedback in adult ADHD, and examined standard versus personalised training protocols. Following PRISMA guidelines, four databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, Ovid, Web of Science) were searched from 1960 to October 2025 for this PROSPERO-registered review (ID: CRD420251020898). Eligible studies included adults (≥ 18 years) with a formal ADHD diagnosis undergoing EEG neurofeedback. Outcomes comprised symptom severity, cognitive performance, electrophysiology, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I V2. Seven studies (three RCTs, four non-randomised; n = 390) met inclusion criteria. Protocols included theta/beta (n = 1), slow cortical potential (n = 1), alpha downregulation training (n = 1) and personalised approaches guided by individual alpha peak frequency (n = 3) or QEEG profiles (n = 1). Naturalistic and personalised studies reported large symptom reductions, whereas RCTs revealed small, generally non-significant effects relative to controls. Cognitive improvements were inconsistently reported and largely attributable to practice effects. Electrophysiological changes were protocol-specific without convergence across studies. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, small samples, variable controls, inconsistent learning metrics, and risk of bias. Current RCTs do not demonstrate evidence of efficacy over placebo. Blinded, adequately powered trials using standardised learning measures are needed to clarify mechanisms of neurofeedback.

papers.title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.abstract: Current practice for normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) relies on clinical presentation, imaging, and various clinical procedures to determine the need for neurosurgical intervention, specifically the installation of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS). This study aimed to evaluate the utility of a TMS-evoked potential (TEP)-based assessment (Delphi-MD) for predicting sustained response (over one year) to VPS, serving as an ancillary test to the cerebrospinal fluid tap test (CTT). Forty-one patients with possible iNPH underwent Delphi-MD evaluation of wave form adherence (WFA), a composite measure assessing how closely their TEPs resembled an ideal benchmark TEP. Of these, 18 patients received VPS treatment following a multidisciplinary team decision based on standard practice, blinded to the TEP results. Response to the intervention was evaluated over a period of more than one year using the clinical global impression of change (CGIC) scale, in addition to assessments with a 10-meter timed up and go test and the modified Rankin scale. Responders had higher M1L WFA values at baseline (prior to VPS) than non-responders (median 0.51 [95% CI 0.36-0.76], median 0.14 [95% CI -0.02-0.38], respectively p = 0.012). M1L WFA was successful in distinguishing responders (11/18) from non-responders (7/18) with an ROC-AUC of 0.935 [bootstrap 95% CI 0.792-1.00], p < 0.0001. M1L WFA cutoff was established with LOOCV and produced 90.9% sensitivity, 85.7% specificity and 88.9% accuracy. In contrast the CTT result was unsuccessful in predicting shunt responsiveness. This study indicates that higher M1L WFA obtained through Delphi-MD (TMS-EEG), signifies better preservation and functional integrity of the motor network in patients with probable iNPH that had a sustained response to VPS than those that did not. Given replication of results in future independent cohorts, Delphi-MD shows promise as an objective, accurate, and accessible ancillary screening tool for iNPH candidates, prior to referral for VPS treatment. papers.abstract: Background: Pseudo-orthostatic tremor (psOT) is a rare form of tremor of the lower body, triggered by standing, at frequencies lower than 13 Hz. It is believed to be secondary to other neurological disorders in a large proportion of cases. Surface electromyography (sEMG) can identify its core characteristics and differentiate it from other similar disorders such as primary orthostatic tremor (POT) and orthostatic myoclonus (OM). Objectives: Our study aims to illustrate the clinical and neurophysiological features as well as the outcomes and final diagnoses of patients with psOT in a retrospective two-centre cohort. Methods: We retrospectively examined the available clinical and neurophysiological records of 35 consecutive patients with a diagnosis of psOT in the 2022-2026 period. Data on demographics, clinical characteristics, sEMG findings, pharmacological treatments, ancillary investigations and patient reported outcomes were collected. Results: 35 patients with psOT were identified, of which 6 (17%) displayed features consistent with a functional neurological disorder (FND). Among the 29 patients with organic psOT, 21 (72.4%) fulfilled the diagnostic criteria for essential tremor (ET), while an identifiable neurological cause was established in four (13.8%). sEMG findings differed between functional and organic psOT, with the latter often displaying features consistent with weight-bearing hyperkinesias. Conclusions: Our retrospective study suggests that psOT is most often associated with ET, while an identifiable neurological cause was found in a relatively small proportion of patients. We also describe functional psOT as a previously unrecognized clinical presentation of FND.

papers.title: Is Less More? Exploring the Visual Processes of Minimalist and Complex Photography Through Eye Tracking and EEG.
papers.abstract: In a world filled with an overwhelming amount of visual information, the clean and distinctive visual style of minimalist photography stands out. However, empirical research on how minimalist style affects visual cognition and psychological responses remains limited. The present study investigated the effects of photographic style (minimalist versus complex) on viewers' visual behavior, emotional responses, and brainwave state by conducting quantitative psychological experiments. Thirty participants viewed photographs in one of the two styles. Eye-tracking, consumer-grade electroencephalography (EEG), and subjective psychological assessment data were collected, enabling comprehensive evaluation of how the participants looked at, responded to, and emotionally engaged with the images. At the level of visual behavior, minimalism elicited significantly reduced number of fixations and saccades, but the duration of a single fixation is significantly longer, and the heatmap hotspots are highly concentrated, presenting a focused processing pattern of fewer but longer gazes. On a psychological level, minimalism evoked significantly less feeling of complexity and greater relaxation, although there was no significant difference in the aesthetics score between the two styles. In terms of brainwave state, viewing minimalist images resulted in significantly higher attention eSense levels, while the meditation eSense level did not show a significant difference. The results of this study therefore show that minimalist composition may influence the visual search pattern to be more focused, which is compatible with the tendency of simplified organization predicted by the principle of simplification. This study not only deepens the theoretical understanding of the psychological mechanisms of minimalist aesthetics, but also provides practical reference for visual communication and image creation of minimalist composition serving as an effective strategy for guiding the eyes toward the core subject.

papers.title: EEG signature in psychiatrist's subjective experience: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: The Assessment of Clinician's Subjective Experience (ACSE) is a self-report questionnaire developed to evaluate clinicians' subjective experiences during patient interactions. While its psychometric properties and clinical validity have been supported, its neurobiological correlates have not yet been investigated. In this pilot study, two clinicians and ten patients participated in a three-phase protocol comprising: (1) a first clinical interview, (2) ACSE administration, and (3) listening to the audio recording of the first clinical interview. EEG activity was recorded from clinicians during both the first clinical interview and questionnaire administration. Neural data were analyzed in terms of relative power spectral density, node strength, and global efficiency computed from imaginary coherence. Clinicians were psychiatrists, one male and one female. Seven patients were diagnosed with mixed anxiety and depressive disorder, and three with unspecified anxiety disorders. ACSE scores were highest for the Difficulty in attunement and Engagement dimensions, consistent with previous literature. EEG findings revealed dimension-specific and topographically distinct oscillatory patterns for only two ACSE dimensions: Difficulty in Attunement and Engagement. More limited evidence emerged for Disconfirmation. Functional connectivity analyses indicated different network profiles, characterized by differences in global efficiency patterns. Correlational analyses further identified significant associations between ACSE dimensions and EEG-derived features. These preliminary findings provide initial evidence that clinicians' subjective experiences during clinical encounters could be associated with measurable neural signatures, offering a novel perspective on the neurobiological basis of intersubjective processes in clinical settings.

papers.title: The effect of text-picture consistency on memory integration in college students: Evidence from ERPs.
papers.abstract: In multimedia learning, individuals often need to integrate textual and visual information. The neural mechanisms underlying how consistency between text and pictures affects memory integration remain unclear. To examine the effect of text-picture consistency on memory integration in college students and to determine the processing time at which this effect occurs. Totally 28 Chinese college students (nfemale = 20, nmale = 8; Mage = 21.64 ± 2.30) participated in this experiment. An adapted pictorial demonstration paradigm was employed. Participants sequentially learned two pairs of text-picture stem facts (consistent vs. inconsistent), separated by an interval, followed by a recognition test for stem and integrated facts. Behavioural and event-related potential (ERP) data were recorded simultaneously. Under the text-picture consistency condition, college students showed significantly better memory integration performance than under the inconsistency condition (58% vs. 48%). EEG results showed that the text-picture inconsistency condition (i.e., the picture and text within a single stem fact were semantically mismatched) elicited a larger P600 wave (500-800 ms) than the text-picture consistency condition, suggesting that text-picture inconsistency primarily induces conflict and integration difficulties during late cognitive processing. No significant differences were observed in the early N400 component. Text-picture consistency facilitates memory integration primarily during late processing, aligning with cognitive theories of multimedia learning. Educationally, it serves as a key quality indicator for multimedia material design. Instructors should prioritize semantic alignment and assess knowledge integration during evaluation.

papers.title: Early neurocognitive outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation.
papers.abstract: Characterization of early neuropsychological outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RFTHC) is essential to guide patient expectations around return to work, study, and caregiving. The current study aimed to describe the early neurocognitive sequelae of SEEG. Consecutive patients undergoing SEEG were prospectively recruited from two tertiary epilepsy centers in Melbourne, Australia. Patients were administered the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS) via telehealth before and 3 weeks after SEEG (M = 19.69 days, SD = 4.41). Given the telehealth platform, the coding subtest was substituted for the Symbol Digit Modalities Test, and a modified score of global cognitive function was calculated. To evaluate group changes, paired sample t-tests were performed. Reliable change indices were computed to explore individual-level changes. Pearson's correlation coefficients evaluated relationships between change in global cognitive function and SEEG admission variables. SEEG patients were invited to complete a semi-structured interview canvassing the recovery following SEEG. Twenty-eight patients completed the neuropsychological examination (M = 37.89 years, SD = 9.72, range = 17-56 years, 54% female). All patients underwent RFTHC with a mean of 11.43 (SD = 6.87, range = 2-28) coagulation sites. At a whole group level, 3-weeks post SEEG there was no evidence for global nor domain-specific cognitive change. Reliable change indices with 90% confidence revealed only 4% (1/28) declined on at least two measures and 10% (3/28) showed psychometric improvement. Pearson's correlational coefficients showed no evidence for association between change in global cognitive function with SEEG factors including admission length, number of spontaneous or stimulated seizures, number of electrodes, or number of RFTHC sites. Subjective reports of language change tended to be accompanied by a decline on the RBANS language index that did not meet reliable change criteria. Most patients reported returning to work around 4 weeks post SEEG. By 3 weeks, gross cognitive functioning tends to be in keeping with pre-SEEG performances for most patients. These findings have direct clinical implications for SEEG neuropsychological counseling. SEEG is increasingly used to guide epilepsy surgery. Despite this, little is known about the cognitive recovery in the weeks following the procedure. We found that for most patients, broad cognitive functioning 3 weeks after SEEG with coagulation was consistent with function before SEEG, with only a small minority showing significant changes. Some people who reported language difficulties also showed a decline on language testing, although this was often small. Of those patients working before SEEG, most returned to work by 4 weeks. These results provide important evidence to guide patient counseling, recovery planning, and management after SEEG.

papers.title: The translational asymmetry of corpus callosotomy: Two literatures that answered different questions.
papers.abstract: Corpus callosotomy is an established palliative operation for drug-resistant epilepsy dominated by drop attacks, and it is performed in three extents: anterior, usually of the anterior two-thirds; total, in one or two stages; and selective posterior, which preserves the genu and rostral body. Meta-analysis finds no difference between them in overall seizure reduction, a difference in drop attack control favoring the posterior approach, and a graded difference in disconnection syndrome, but there has never been a prospective head-to-head comparison, and the optimal extent of section remains undefined. A search of PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection identified 62 experimental studies in which the corpus callosum or another forebrain commissure was sectioned with an epilepsy-related outcome, spanning 1948-2026 across six species and every major seizure model. This literature is neither absent nor recent. What it has almost never done is vary the extent of section: the few studies that varied it took the laterality of kindling transfer or of interictal synchrony as the endpoint, never seizure control and never cognitive cost. No study compares the three extents against a common outcome; none models the selective posterior operation as it is defined clinically; none randomizes between extents; and none combines graded disconnection with time-locked bilateral electrophysiology, diffusion-based verification of the fibers divided, and a behavioral read-out in the same animals. The effect of section is also bidirectional: focal seizures may intensify through loss of transcallosal inhibition, and in the pentylenetetrazol model callosal section paradoxically facilitates convulsions, which limits chemoconvulsant preparations. The asymmetry between the clinical and experimental literatures is therefore one of method rather than of volume or attention: the two answered different questions, and the question the clinical field now asks requires a manipulation the experimental literature has never performed. PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Surgeons can treat severe epilepsies by cutting the bundle of fibers that joins the two halves of the brain, but they do not agree on how much of it to cut. We searched three databases and found 62 animal studies of this operation going back to 1948. Almost none of them compared different amounts of cutting, and none looked at the newest version of the operation. Answering the surgeons' question will require a new kind of animal experiment rather than more reading of the old ones.

papers.title: Acupotomy Alleviates Pain and Attenuates Spinal Neuronal Hyperexcitability in Knee Osteoarthritis Rats: Implication of the CaMKII/GluA1 Axis.
papers.abstract: To investigate the spinal mechanisms underlying the analgesic effects of acupotomy on chronic pain and central sensitization in rats with monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Following MIA-induced KOA and a three-week acupotomy intervention in rats, pain behaviors and joint pathology were assessed. Spinal RNA-sequencing was performed to identify differentially expressed genes. Key targets (CaMKII and GluA1) were validated at both mRNA and protein levels using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Furthermore, immunofluorescence and whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology were employed to evaluate the activation and excitability of spinal substantia gelatinosa (SG) neurons. Acupotomy significantly alleviated mechanical and thermal hyperalgesia and reduced joint degeneration in KOA rats. RNA-seq analysis revealed the modulation of 220 genes in the spinal cord. These DEGs were significantly enriched in calcium signaling and synaptic transmission pathways, highlighting CaMKII and Gria1 as potential key molecules. Molecular validations confirmed that acupotomy downregulated CaMKII and Gria1 mRNA expression and the phosphorylation ratios of CaMKII and GluA1. Furthermore, acupotomy reduced the activation of p-CaMKII-positive neurons in the spinal SG region and dampened their abnormally high-frequency action potential discharges. Acupotomy intervention ameliorates peripheral joint degeneration and exerts significant analgesia in KOA, which is accompanied by a reduction in the intrinsic hyperexcitability of spinal SG neurons. Although direct causal validation utilizing targeted inhibitors is warranted, our findings suggest that this analgesic effect is closely associated with the downregulation of the CaMKII/GluA1 signaling axis, providing a plausible central mechanistic framework.
